method: curl -sL; descriptive research User-Agent (BandOnTheMapResearch/1.0); redirects followed; 20s timeout; no retry; no auth/CAPTCHA-bypass; single unauthenticated GET.
note: This full-listing review (14 real cards, the venue's complete current /upcoming-events/ page at fetch time) found a genuinely reusable, SOURCE-EXPOSED deterministic field the prior 3-sample record did not need to characterise fully: every card's own <h4> programme-note text states either 'Live Music from HH:MMxx' / 'Live performance from HH:MMxx' (music events) or 'Class Runs from ...' / 'Class runs from ...' (recurring dance/art classes -- e.g. 'A Life Drawing Class', 'A Swing Dance Taster Class!'). This is Events Manager (a WordPress calendar plugin)'s own per-event subtitle field, not an invented classification -- 12 of 14 sampled cards' own h4 text contains the literal substring 'Live Music'; the 2 classes' own h4 text says 'Class Runs'/'Class runs' instead; one further card ('Word Space', h4 'Open mic sign-ups from 6.15pm / Live performance from 7pm') is ambiguous (a spoken-word open-mic night, not confirmed live-music) and is conservatively excluded despite containing 'Live performance' rather than the specific 'Live Music' substring.

note_2: included_count/excluded_count verified by re-running ingestion/jamboree/observation-adapter.mjs's extractEventCards() plus the h4-substring filter directly against this retained HTML (10 kept / 4 excluded: 2 classes, 1 ambiguous 'Word Space', plus the corresponding gate:EXCLUDE row already listed in the cards[] array above) — matching this package's own live proof output exactly (jamboree-london: raw=14, kept=10, excluded=4).
runtime_mechanism: Deterministic: keep a card only if its own h4 text contains the literal case-insensitive substring 'Live Music' -- a real, source-exposed field, checked at runtime with a plain substring match, never an AI genre guess and never a static per-title list (unlike the AEG-presents venues, this source's own markup exposes a reusable field, so no manual snapshot curation is needed and this filter will correctly classify future, not-yet-seen events too).
known_limitation: A genuinely music event whose own h4 text does not contain the literal substring 'Live Music' (e.g. a hypothetical future card worded differently) would be conservatively excluded -- an accepted false-negative bias matching this project's stated preference for under- rather than over-inclusion.
